mainTopic: Is the juice inside impure grapes 'stored' or 'absorbed', and the concern for תקלה when burning impure תרומה
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier discussion: the word ״ראשית״ teaches that תרומה takes effect only when the owner is left with a usable remainder. Then רב אחא בר רב עויא quotes רבי יוחנן: impure grapes may be pressed less than a כביצה at a time, and the wine stays pure, even for נסכים. The reason is that רבי יוחנן holds the juice is only 'stored' in the grape (מיפקד פקידי), so it meets impurity only when squeezed out, when too little impure food is present. רב חסדא rejects this, because he holds the juice is 'absorbed' (מיבלע בליעי) and became impure together with the grape. רב אחא challenges him from a משנה about squeezing an exact כביצה. רב חסדא answers that the משנה speaks of grapes that were never made susceptible to impurity. He then tries to prove his view from a ברייתא saying impure תרומה grapes cannot be eaten. רבא deflects the proof: that ban may be just a גזירה against תקלה, and he defends this against אביי's challenge from burning impure bread and oil. Finally the גמרא examines that ברייתא: one view allows burning only bread, not wheat, while רבי יוחנן allows even wheat. The answer to why he does not worry about תקלה begins with רב אשי's statement and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The verse 'ראשית' requires usable leftovers
steps.stepSummary: The closing answer of an earlier discussion: ״ראשית״ means תרומה takes effect only when the remainder can be used by a ישראל. So separating תרומה from produce whose remainder is unusable does not work.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: The verse says 'ראשית' (the first part). This means the leftovers must be recognizable (usable) for a ישראל. That excludes this case, where the leftovers are not usable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a discussion from the previous part of the דף by giving a verse-based reason. It explains why a certain separation of תרומה does not take effect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ״ראשית״ (the first) implies there is a 'rest' left over that the owner can use. If the remaining produce cannot be used at all, as with חמץ on פסח, there is no real 'first part', so the separation is not valid תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The first part', the verse's word for תרומה
Its leftovers / remainder
Recognizable, meaning usable as a remainder
This case is excluded

steps.whatToRemember: תרומה only works when separating it leaves a usable remainder for the owner. That rule comes from the word ״ראשית״.

phrases.english: He said: the verse states 'the first'
phrases.notes: Deuteronomy 18:4, about giving the first of your grain, wine and oil

phrases.english: meaning that its leftovers are recognizable for an Israelite,
which excludes this case, whose leftovers are not recognizable.
phrases.notes: For example, חמץ on פסח, where the remainder is forbidden

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes a discussion that began on the previous amud
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The verse ״ראשית״ requires that the leftovers be usable, so where they are not usable, the תרומה does not take effect.

steps.title: Impure grapes may be pressed in small amounts
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר רב עויא quotes רבי יוחנן: impure grapes may be trodden less than a כביצה at a time, and the wine is fit even for נסכים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר רב עויא sat before רב חסדא and said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Grapes that became impure may be trodden less than an egg-bulk at a time, and their wine is kosher even for libations on the altar.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins with a ruling from רבי יוחנן about pressing impure grapes. He says the wine can come out pure if you press only small amounts at a time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food passes on impurity only if it is at least a כביצה (the size of an egg). By pressing less than that, the impure grape flesh is too small to make the juice impure. So the wine is pure enough even for the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: Grapes that became ritually impure
He treads (presses) them
An egg-bulk, the minimum size for food to transmit impurity
Wine libations poured on the altar

steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling is the base for the whole debate that follows about how juice inside fruit relates to the fruit itself.

phrases.aramaic: יָתֵיב רַב אַחָא בַּר רַב עַוְיָא
phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Rav Avya sat
before Rav Chisda,
and he sat and said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
Grapes that became impure —
one treads them in amounts each less than an egg-bulk,
and their wine is fit for libations.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָתֵיב רַב אַחָא בַּר רַב עַוְיָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב חִסְדָּא, וְיָתֵיב וְאָמַר מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Impure grapes pressed less than a כביצה at a time produce wine that is pure and fit for נסכים.

steps.title: The reasoning: juice is just stored inside the grape
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers that רבי יוחנן holds משקין מיפקד פקידי. The juice is not part of the grape, so it becomes impure only when squeezed out, and by then there is less than a כביצה of food to make it impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: So it seems he holds that liquids are 'stored' inside the fruit. When do they become impure? Only when he squeezes them out. And when he squeezes them, the impure food is less than the minimum size.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what principle stands behind רבי יוחנן's ruling. It says he views the juice as sitting inside the grape like liquid in a container.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the juice is only 'stored', the grape's impurity did not soak into it. The juice can catch impurity only when it touches the impure flesh while coming out. If the flesh being pressed is under a כביצה, it is too small to transmit impurity, so the juice stays pure.

keyTerms.meaning: Apparently / it follows that
He holds (this view)
Liquids are stored (deposited) inside the fruit, separate from it
He squeezes
Required minimum measure

steps.confusionAlert: The grape itself really is impure. The point is only that the juice inside is treated as a separate item that has not become impure yet, not that the grape is pure.

phrases.english: Apparently he holds:
liquids are stored inside the fruit,
so when do they become impure?
When he squeezes them out.
And when he squeezes them, the food is not at its minimum measure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the underlying principle of רבי יוחנן's ruling
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוחנן, juice is stored in the fruit and becomes impure only when squeezed. At that moment less than a כביצה of impure food is involved.

steps.title: Why not a full egg-bulk? A משנה permits it
steps.stepSummary: If this reasoning is right, even an exact כביצה should be fine. Indeed a משנה rules that a טמא מת who squeezed exactly a כביצה of olives or grapes produces pure liquid.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, even an egg-bulk should be allowed! For we learned in a משנה: A person impure from a corpse who squeezed olives or grapes, exactly an egg-bulk, the liquid is pure!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's limit of 'less than' a כביצה. It argues that the same logic allows a full כביצה, as a משנה clearly says.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With an exact כביצה, as soon as the first drop comes out, the remaining food is already less than a כביצה. So the juice should still be pure. The משנה confirms this, which makes רבי יוחנן's stricter limit look unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
For we learned in a משנה
A person impure from contact with a corpse
Exact, precisely measured

phrases.english: If so, an egg-bulk too should be allowed?
For we learned in a mishna:
One impure from a corpse who squeezed olives and grapes
an exact egg-bulk — they (the liquids) are pure!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the precise measure in רבי יוחנן's ruling
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's requirement of less than a כביצה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His own reasoning, backed by a משנה, permits an exact כביצה, so why limit it to less?

steps.title: After the fact versus from the start
steps.stepSummary: The משנה describes the case after the fact (דיעבד). רבי יוחנן is giving guidance for the start (לכתחלה), and adds a גזירה so a person does not end up pressing more than a כביצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, the משנה is speaking about after it was done. Here, רבי יוחנן is speaking about what to do in the first place. It is a decree, lest he come to press more than an egg-bulk.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by separating two situations. One is what is valid after the act was done, and the other is what one should plan to do from the start.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Strictly, an exact כביצה keeps the juice pure, so the משנה rules it pure after the fact. But the חכמים told people to press less than a כביצה from the start. Aiming for exactly a כביצה might lead someone to go slightly over, and then the juice would become impure.

keyTerms.meaning: If he already did it (after the fact, דיעבד)
From the outset, ideally
A rabbinic protective decree
Lest / perhaps

steps.whatToRemember: An exact כביצה works after the fact. From the start, one presses less than a כביצה, as a safeguard against going over.

phrases.english: There — it is when he already did it,
here — it is from the outset.
It is a decree, lest he come
to do more than an egg-bulk.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge from the משנה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing דיעבד from לכתחלה, plus a rabbinic גזירה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן's 'less than a כביצה' seemed to conflict with the משנה allowing an exact כביצה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה rules after the fact. רבי יוחנן sets a stricter rule for the start, out of concern that a person will exceed a כביצה.

steps.title: רב חסדא: where did the impurity go?
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא sharply rejects רבי יוחנן's ruling. He asks rhetorically where the impurity that was in the grapes could have gone.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said to him: Who will listen to you and to your teacher רבי יוחנן? The impurity that was in the grapes, where did it go?
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא attacks the whole basis of רבי יוחנן's ruling. His question 'where did it go?' is rhetorical: the impurity is still in the juice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not an attack on a detail like the כביצה measure. It denies the core idea that the juice could ever be pure. In רב חסדא's view, the juice already shared the grapes' impurity before any squeezing.

keyTerms.meaning: Who will listen to you? (a sharp rejection)
Your teacher
Where did it go?

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said to him:

phrases.aramaic: מַאן צָיֵית לָךְ וּלְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן רַבָּךְ?
phrases.english: Who will listen to you and to Rabbi Yochanan your teacher?
The impurity that was in them, where did it go?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב חִסְדָּא: מַאן צָיֵית לָךְ וּלְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן רַבָּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the entire ruling from steps 2 and 3, not just the measure
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that the wine of impure grapes can be pure
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The grapes' impurity must already be in the juice, so pressing small amounts cannot help.

steps.title: רב חסדא's view: juice is absorbed into the grape
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers that רב חסדא holds משקין מיבלע בליעי. The juice is part of the grape, so when the grape became impure, the juice became impure with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: So it seems he holds that liquids are absorbed in the fruit. And since the food became impure, the liquids also became impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the principle behind רב חסדא's objection. It sets up a clear contrast with רבי יוחנן's 'stored' view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the juice is absorbed and part of the grape, it became impure the moment the grape did. Squeezing in small amounts changes nothing, because the juice was impure before pressing began. This is the exact opposite of רבי יוחנן's principle.

keyTerms.meaning: Liquids are absorbed into the fruit, as part of it
The food (the grape flesh)
They became impure

steps.whatToRemember: The core dispute: רבי יוחנן holds משקין מיפקד פקידי (juice is stored, separate), while רב חסדא holds משקין מיבלע בליעי (juice is absorbed, part of the fruit).
steps.whyThisMatters: The 'stored versus absorbed' question decides whether impure fruit can ever produce pure juice. The principle reaches beyond this case of grapes.

phrases.english: Apparently he holds:
liquids are absorbed in the fruit.
And since the food became impure,
the liquids became impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלְמָא קָא סָבַר: מַשְׁקִין מִיבְלָע בְּלִיעִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the principle behind רב חסדא's objection and contrasts it with step 3
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רב חסדא, juice is absorbed in the fruit, so impure grapes mean impure juice.

steps.title: Challenge to רב חסדא from the משנה of the exact כביצה
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא asks רב חסדא: the משנה says that a טמא מת who squeezed exactly a כביצה of olives or grapes produces pure juice. That only makes sense if the juice is 'stored' (מיפקד פקידי). If it is 'absorbed' (מיבלע בליעי), why is it pure?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Don't you agree that liquids are stored inside the fruit? We learned in a משנה: a person impure from a corpse who squeezed olives or grapes of exactly a כביצה, the juice is pure. If you say the juice is stored, that is why it is pure. But if you say it is absorbed, why should it be pure?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב חסדא's view (step 7) by quoting the same משנה used earlier in step 4.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the juice is part of the grape (מיבלע בליעי), then when the טמא מת touched the grapes, the juice became impure along with them. Yet the משנה says the juice is pure. That fits only with משקין מיפקד פקידי, which is רבי יוחנן's view, so the משנה seems to disprove רב חסדא.

keyTerms.meaning: Stored separately: the juice sits inside the fruit like something deposited there, and is not part of the fruit.
Absorbed: the juice is soaked into the fruit and counts as part of it.
'But didn't we learn in a משנה...?' This introduces a challenge from a משנה.
Exactly measured, with no more and no less.
'Granted / it works well if...' This sets up a contrast: one view fits, the other does not.

phrases.english: He said to him: And don't you hold
that liquids are stored inside?
But we learned: one impure from a corpse who squeezed
phrases.notes: The same משנה cited in step 4.

phrases.english: olives or grapes, exactly an egg-volume, they (the liquids) are pure.
Granted, if you say they are stored,
that is why they are pure;
but if you say they are absorbed,
why are they pure?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַתְּ לָא תִּיסְבְּרָא דְּמַשְׁקִין מִיפְקָד פְּקִידִי? וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the inference in step 7 that רב חסדא holds משקין מיבלע בליעי.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's position that juice is absorbed (מיבלע בליעי).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under the absorbed view, impure grapes would make their juice impure. The משנה rules the juice pure, so the absorbed view seems to contradict the משנה.

steps.title: The משנה speaks of grapes never made susceptible to impurity
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא answers that the משנה deals with grapes that were never הוכשרו (made susceptible to impurity by being wetted). They become susceptible only while being squeezed, and by then less than a כביצה is left.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: What case are we dealing with here? Grapes that were not yet made susceptible to impurity. When do they become susceptible? When he squeezes them. And once he squeezes them, they are less than the required amount.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא defends himself by narrowing the משנה to a special case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food can become impure only after liquid has wetted it (הכשר). These grapes were dry, so the טמא מת's touch did nothing at first. The squeezing wets them with their own juice, but by then the grape mass is already below a כביצה. That is too small to pass impurity on to the juice, so the juice stays pure even on the absorbed view.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What case are we dealing with here?' This narrows a source to a specific situation.
Were made susceptible to impurity (הֶכְשֵׁר), which happens through contact with liquid.
Lacking or reduced.
The minimum required measure (here a כביצה).

steps.confusionAlert: Touching food does not automatically make it impure. Food first needs הכשר, meaning it must have been wet by liquid. That is the whole key to this answer.

phrases.english: He said to him: With what are we dealing here?
With grapes that were not made susceptible.
When do they become susceptible? When he squeezes them.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי סָחֵיט לְהוּ — בְּצִיר לְהוּ שִׁיעוּרָא.
phrases.english: When he squeezes them, they are lacking the measure.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא): the משנה deals only with grapes that were not yet הוכשרו.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to speak of ordinary grapes that were already susceptible to impurity, which would prove the juice is stored.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה speaks of dry grapes. Their susceptibility begins only when squeezing starts, when less than a כביצה remains, so the משנה fits the absorbed view too.

steps.title: Support from the ברייתא that impure תרומה grapes cannot be eaten
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא argues his reading must be right. A ברייתא says impure תרומה of berries and grapes has no permitted eating use. If juice were 'stored', one could tread them less than a כביצה at a time and drink pure juice.
steps.simpleTranslation: For if you do not say this, there is the ברייתא: 'To what is this similar? To impure תרומה of berries (olives) and grapes, which has neither permission to eat nor permission to burn.' But it does have permission to eat, since if he wants he can tread them less than a כביצה at a time!
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא brings a ברייתא to show that the juice must be absorbed, which supports his own view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If juice were stored separately, as רבי יוחנן holds, impure תרומה grapes could be trodden less than a כביצה at a time, and the juice would come out pure and drinkable. The ברייתא says there is no eating permission at all. That suggests the juice is absorbed and impure along with the grapes.

keyTerms.meaning: 'For if you do not say so...' This introduces a proof that the previous claim must be correct.
The portion of produce given to a כהן. Once impure it may not be eaten.
A permitted use by eating.
A permitted use as fuel for burning.
Treads or presses (grapes).

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִי לָא תֵּימָא הָכִי, הָא דְּתַנְיָא:
phrases.english: For if you do not say so, that which was taught in a ברייתא:
To what is this similar?
To תרומה of berries (olives) and grapes that became impure,
phrases.notes: The parenthetical is a textual variant.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין לוֹ בָּהּ לֹא הֶיתֵּר אֲכִילָה
phrases.english: for which he has neither permission to eat
nor permission to burn.

phrases.aramaic: הָא הֶיתֵּר אֲכִילָה נָמֵי אִית בֵּיהּ,
phrases.english: But it does have permission to eat too,
since if he wishes he can tread them
less than a כביצה at a time.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי לָא תֵּימָא הָכִי, הָא דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens the answer in step 9 by showing that the stored view clashes with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That the juice is absorbed (מיבלע בליעי), so the משנה must be read as dry grapes.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא stating that impure תרומה grapes have no permission to be eaten or burned.

steps.title: The ברייתא may reflect only a rabbinic decree
steps.stepSummary: רבא deflects the proof. Even if the juice is stored, the חכמים forbade treading impure תרומה grapes in small amounts, because the person might come to a mishap (תקלה) and eat it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It is a rabbinic decree, lest he come to a mishap with them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא blocks רב חסדא's proof from the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's statement 'no eating permission' may not be a rule about how juice works. It may be a rabbinic גזירה: if someone keeps impure תרומה grapes to press later, he might forget and eat them. So the ברייתא no longer proves מיבלע בליעי.

keyTerms.meaning: A protective rabbinic decree.
A stumbling block or mishap, here accidentally eating something forbidden.
Perhaps, lest.

phrases.english: רבא said: It is a decree, lest
he come through them to a mishap.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: גְּזֵירָה דִּילְמָא אָתֵי בְּהוּ לִידֵי תַקָּלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 10.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from the ברייתא is rejected. It does not decide whether juice is stored or absorbed.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ban on eating may come from a rabbinic גזירה about תקלה, not from the nature of the juice.

steps.title: אביי asks: do we really worry about תקלה?
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רבא from a ברייתא that permits lighting a fire with impure תרומה bread and oil. That suggests no worry that someone will end up eating them.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Do we worry about a mishap? But it was taught: one may light with bread and oil of תרומה that became impure.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רבא's idea of a גזירה because of תקלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the חכמים feared that a person keeping impure תרומה would accidentally eat it, they should have forbidden keeping impure bread and oil for fuel too. Since the ברייתא permits it, it seems we do not worry about תקלה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And do we worry...?' This is a challenging rhetorical question.
'But it was taught in a ברייתא...' This introduces a contradicting source.
One may light (a fire or lamp).

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: וּמִי חָיְישִׁינַן לְתַקָּלָה?
phrases.english: אביי said to him: And do we worry about a mishap?
But it was taught:
One may light with bread and with oil
of תרומה that became impure.

steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that the חכמים decreed because of תקלה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא allows keeping and burning impure תרומה bread and oil without any fear of accidental eating, so תקלה seems not to be a concern.

steps.title: Bread and oil are made unappetizing first
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the ברייתא allows burning only when the food is made unattractive. The bread is thrown among the wood, and the oil is put in a disgusting vessel, so no one will eat it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The bread, he throws it among the wood. The תרומה oil, he puts it in a repulsive vessel.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends his concern for תקלה by explaining how the ברייתא avoids it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We do worry about תקלה. In the ברייתא's case the risk is removed because the food is spoiled or placed somewhere disgusting before burning. With grapes kept for pressing there is no such safeguard, so the גזירה stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Throws.
Among the firewood.
A repulsive or disgusting vessel.

phrases.english: He said to him: Bread,
he throws it among the wood.
Oil of תרומה,
he puts it into a repulsive vessel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: פַּת זָרֵיק לֵיהּ בֵּין הָעֵצִים
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining the case: the ברייתא assumes safeguards that remove the תקלה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to allow burning impure תרומה with no precautions, implying no fear of תקלה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Burning is allowed only after the food is made unappealing, so concern for תקלה remains valid.
steps.whatToRemember: The question of stored vs. absorbed juice is left without proof from the ברייתא. רבא shows it may reflect only a גזירה of תקלה, and we do worry about תקלה unless the food is made unappealing.

steps.title: חזקיה and רב הונא: only bread may be burned, not wheat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the ברייתא about lighting with impure תרומה. אביי quotes it in the name of חזקיה, and רבא quotes it from the school of רבי יצחק בר מרתא in the name of רב הונא: the permission covers bread only, not wheat, out of concern for תקלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The matter itself: one may light with impure תרומה bread and oil. אביי said in the name of חזקיה, and רבא said that the school of רבי יצחק בר מרתא said in the name of רב הונא: They taught this only about bread, but not wheat, lest he come to a mishap with it.
steps.whatsHappening: Using the word גופא, the גמרא opens a new discussion of the ברייתא it just quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bread thrown among the wood gets ruined. Wheat kernels can stay edible, so a person might take them and eat them. Therefore רב הונא limits the permission to bread.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The matter itself': the גמרא returns to examine a source quoted in passing.
In the name of.
'They taught this only about...' This limits a ruling.
Wheat kernels.

phrases.english: The matter itself: one may light with bread
and with oil of תרומה that became impure.
אביי said in the name of חזקיה,

phrases.aramaic: וְרָבָא אָמַר דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר מָרְתָא
phrases.english: and רבא said in the name of the school of רבי יצחק בר מרתא
that רב הונא said:
They taught this only about bread;
but wheat, no,
lest he come through them to a mishap.

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא: מַדְלִיקִין בְּפַת וּבְשֶׁמֶן שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה שֶׁנִּטְמֵאת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the ברייתא quoted in step 12 and analyzes it on its own.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Impure תרומה may be burned only as bread, not as wheat kernels, because of the risk of תקלה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: even wheat may be burned
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן disagrees with רב הונא and allows burning even impure תרומה wheat.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: Even wheat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the opposing view to רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן extends the ברייתא's permission to wheat kernels. He does not seem bothered by the concern for תקלה that drove רב הונא's limit, which sets up the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: Even.
The great אמורא of ארץ ישראל, here disagreeing with רב הונא.

phrases.english: And רבי יוחנן said: Even wheat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes רב הונא's limitation in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Impure תרומה wheat may also be used as fuel.

steps.title: Why isn't רבי יוחנן worried about תקלה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יוחנן permits wheat. We should worry that the person will come to eat it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why? Let us worry that he might come through them to a mishap!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's permission for wheat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wheat thrown among wood is not ruined the way bread is. So the same concern for תקלה that רבא and רב הונא accepted should forbid it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Let us be concerned.'
Comes (to).
Into the hands of, to the point of.

phrases.english: And why? Let us worry lest
he come through them to a mishap!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַמַּאי? נֵיחוּשׁ דִּילְמָא אָתֵי בָּהֶן לִידֵי תַּקָּלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's ruling in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's permission to burn impure תרומה wheat.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Wheat stays edible among the firewood, so the accepted concern for תקלה should forbid it.

steps.title: The answer begins with רב אשי's principle
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts to answer by citing a statement of רב אשי. The content continues on the next amud.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is about to answer the question about רבי יוחנן by borrowing an idea רב אשי said elsewhere, and that idea comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase כדאמר signals that the answer is not new. It applies a known statement of רב אשי to this case. We must wait for the next lines to see how it removes the worry of תקלה for wheat.

keyTerms.meaning: 'As (so-and-so) said.' This applies an existing statement to the current problem.
A late אמורא, a central editor of the תלמוד בבלי.

phrases.english: As רב אשי said:
phrases.notes: Setup; the content continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the answer to the question in step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Applying an outside principle from רב אשי (the content follows on the next amud).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן seems to ignore the danger of תקלה with wheat.
steps.terutzMaskana: The answer will rest on רב אשי's statement, given on the next amud.
